item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russia continues missile and sabotage attacks inside Ukraine, including a ballistic strike on Kyiv that killed one civilian and injured fourteen, and a fire near a weapons factory blamed on a Russia-run network. Ukrainian forces are conducting deep-strike missions up to 2,500 km, hitting a missile-battery plant in Yelets and a chemical plant in Voronezh, and are evacuating wounded soldiers by drone. A US-brokered ceasefire is now in effect in the occupied city of Oleshky, where residents previously survived on weeds. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israeli forces have intensified a crackdown in Hebron, displacing thousands and prompting UN warnings of ethnic cleansing, while IDF raids have expelled farmers and settlers have attacked olive pickers. The Israeli election sees record turnout, with Palestinians in the West Bank fearing further violence if Netanyahu remains prime minister and some uncertain whether to vote or boycott. Settlers are looking beyond Netanyahu to the far right, and Arab parties accuse Netanyahu of inciting hatred to scare voters. The conflict has produced 21,440 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iran and the regional confrontation: the situation
item.description:
Iran is intensifying threats to the region, urging the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz while Houthi missiles and drones continue striking Saudi oil facilities and airports, prompting the reopening of Riyadh Airport after weeks of disruption. Qatar is urging Iran to end these threats and reopen the strait, while Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials are preparing talks with Iran to defuse tensions. The United States is considering renewed strikes on Iran, driving oil prices above $117 a barrel. Iran’s Supreme Leader and top security chief discussed war and Hormuz, and the Saudi-led coalition reported downing Houthi missiles and drones aimed at the kingdom. 123 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:

Syrian authorities report civilian casualties from the Jordanian attacks. The Jordanian government maintains the operations are aimed at militants, while families of the victims deny any connection to the church attack. 2,732 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
Iraqi courts have sentenced six French nationals to life imprisonment and a seventh to 15 years for Islamic State membership, while another court imposed lengthy terms on seven French citizens for the same crime. Security forces have repeatedly intercepted unidentified drones over Baghdad's Green Zone, with multiple incidents reported. Yazidi militia units linked to the PKK are disarming and joining the Iraqi army, and three militia groups have pledged to disarm by June 2027. Iran has intensified rhetoric warning the United States, and the United States has warned Baghdad it will strike Iraqi militias that join Iran's war. The conflict produced 396 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.description:
Intensified drone attacks by the Rapid Support Forces have hit Nyala, killing at least 21 people, injuring 40 and knocking out power in southeast Sudan, worsening civilian hardship. The Sudanese Armed Forces and allied militias continue to grind the conflict, while women under siege are increasingly acting as frontline responders to meet basic needs. Hundreds of thousands of Sudanese refugees are now hosted in Chad as the regional humanitarian emergency expands. The United Nations warns of a looming famine risk as the war grinds on, and the conflict caused 4,680 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

The government partnered with Israel's Gilat to provide nationwide satellite internet and secured a UNESCO world-heritage nomination for the Boma-Bandingilo inscription. Governor Dollar promoted the reintegration of IDPs and returnees, and the U.S. Embassy remembered staff who died supporting South Sudanese people. 2 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:

Fitgharan forces now control the Mogadishu-Baidoa corridor and Laftagareen forces have seized Buurhakaba and a town in Bay, extending combat in the south. Ethiopia has withdrawn over 3,000 troops and will not intervene in the South West State conflict. Kidnappers abducted six residents in Kaduna's Millennium City estate and three vigilantes died in a separate Plateau incident. item.title: Pakistan and Afghanistan: the situation
item.description:

The closure has driven an unprecedented rise in LPG prices, which the Pakistani minister attributes to the border shutdown, and the government has launched an operation against illegal Afghans in Peshawar and banned gatherings in Balochistan's Pishin ahead of an intensified campaign. Pakistan accuses the Taliban of using Afghan territory to launch attacks against it, while the Taliban government has reshuffled civilian and military officials in Badakhshan.
